# Priority Expiry LRU Cache

<!-- meta:begin -->
| Format | Difficulty | Asked at | Round | Topics | Last reported |

| Object Oriented Programming | Hard | Tesla | Phone screen | — | Aug 2025 |

> **▶ [Solve it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/questions/priority-expire-cache-eviction)** — free, no card: a runnable editor, the sample and hidden tests, a judged verdict, and the reference solution.

## Problem

Design a cache called `PriorityExpiryLRUCache` that associates keys with values, and also tracks a priority and an expiration time for each entry. The cache can hold at most `capacity` elements at any moment. When the cache is full and a new entry needs to be added, the eviction policy selects one victim by applying a strict hierarchy of rules — first considering expiry, then priority, and finally recency of access.

Internally, every cached entry stores:
- `value`
- `priority`
- `expiryTime`
- `lastAccessedTime`

The `lastAccessedTime` is refreshed whenever an entry is:
- inserted for the first time,
- updated via a repeated `set` call,
- or successfully returned by `get`.

Implement the `PriorityExpiryLRUCache` class with the following methods:

- `PriorityExpiryLRUCache(int capacity)`
  Constructs a cache with the given maximum `capacity`.

- `void set(String key, String value, int priority, int expiryTime, int currentTime)`
  Inserts a new entry or updates an existing one.
  - When `key` already exists in the cache, replace its `value`, `priority`, and `expiryTime`.
  - When `key` is absent and the cache has reached its `capacity`, a single entry must be evicted according to the eviction hierarchy before the new entry can be inserted.
  - After the insertion or update completes, record the entry’s `lastAccessedTime` as `currentTime`.

- `String get(String key, int currentTime)`
  Returns the value bound to `key`.
  - If `key` is not found, return an empty string `""`.
  - If the entry is expired (`expiryTime ≤ currentTime`), remove it from the cache and return `""`.
  - Otherwise, set the entry’s `lastAccessedTime` to `currentTime` and return its value.

- `String evictItem(int currentTime)`
  Removes exactly one entry from the cache according to the following layered rules and returns the removed key. If the cache is empty, return `""`.
  1. **Expiry First**: if any entries satisfy `expiryTime ≤ currentTime`, evict one of the expired entries; among the expired entries, choose the one with the earliest `expiryTime`.
  2. **Priority Second**: if no entry is expired, evict the entry with the smallest `priority` value.
  3. **LRU Tie-breaker**: if several entries share that same lowest priority, evict the one whose `lastAccessedTime` is the smallest (the Least Recently Used entry).

Constraints:

- `1 ≤ capacity, priority ≤ 10^4`
- `0 ≤ expiryTime, currentTime ≤ 10^5`
- The total number of method invocations will not exceed `10^5`.

Example:

> **Input:**
> ["PriorityExpiryLRUCache","set","set","set","evictItem","get","set","evictItem","set","evictItem","get","get","set","get","set","set","set","get"]
[[3],["A","valueA",10,100,10],["B","valueB",5,150,20],["C","valueC",5,200,30],[110],["B",120],["D","valueD",3,300,130],[135],["E","valueE",5,250,140],[145],["Z",145],["B",150],["E","newE",8,400,160],["E",165],["F","valueF",2,500,170],["G","valueG",7,500,175],["H","valueH",6,500,180],["H",185]]
>
> **Output:**
> [null,null,null,null,"A","valueB",null,"D",null,"C","","",null,"newE",null,null,null,"valueH"]
>
> **Explanation:**
> - `PriorityExpiryLRUCache cache = new PriorityExpiryLRUCache(3);`
> - `cache.set("A","valueA",10,100,10);` // Insert A with priority 10, expiry 100.
> - `cache.set("B","valueB",5,150,20);` // Insert B with priority 5, expiry 150.
> - `cache.set("C","valueC",5,200,30);` // Insert C with priority 5, expiry 200.
> - `cache.evictItem(110);` // Returns "A". At time 110, A is expired (100 ≤ 110); expired items are evicted first.
> - `cache.get("B",120);` // Returns "valueB". A successful get updates B's `lastAccessedTime` to 120.
> - `cache.set("D","valueD",3,300,130);` // Insert D with priority 3, expiry 300.
> - `cache.evictItem(135);` // Returns "D". No items are expired at time 135, so the lowest-priority item (D, priority 3) is evicted.
> - `cache.set("E","valueE",5,250,140);` // Insert E with priority 5, expiry 250.
> - `cache.evictItem(145);` // Returns "C". Lowest priority is 5 (B, C, E). Breaking the tie by LRU: C has the smallest `lastAccessedTime`.
> - `cache.get("Z",145);` // Returns "" because key Z is not present.
> - `cache.get("B",150);` // Returns "" and removes B since it is expired at the boundary ($$150 \le 150$$).
> - `cache.set("E","newE",8,400,160);` // Update E’s value/priority/expiry and refresh its `lastAccessedTime` to 160.
> - `cache.get("E",165);` // Returns "newE".
> - `cache.set("F","valueF",2,500,170);` // Insert F with priority 2, expiry 500.
> - `cache.set("G","valueG",7,500,175);` // Insert G with priority 7, expiry 500.
> - `cache.set("H","valueH",6,500,180);` // Cache is full, so an item is automatically evicted before inserting H. No expired items exist; the lowest-priority item F is evicted.
> - `cache.get("H",185);` // Returns "valueH".

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

The eviction policy has three rules in order: expired entries first, then lowest priority, then LRU among same priority.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use a combination of data structures: a priority queue for expiration times, a map for priority groups, and a linked list for LRU within each group.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The tricky part is handling ties in priority, you need to track the least recently used entry among those with the same priority.

</details>
